$comment: The boot path's ceilings (tools/build-site.mjs SITE-10, architecture audit 2026-11-19 item 3): the modules and the gzip bytes a player loads
to the sign-in screen and to the first town, as the default delivery serves them. The ceiling is each stage's LAST row.
It goes up only through node tools/build-site.mjs --boot-path-raise "<why>", which appends a row with its reason; --boot-path-write appends
a lower row after a cut (a cut of more than BOOT_SLACK is red until it is locked in). Written by the tool, never by hand. Two lanes that both
moved a ceiling conflict here: take either side and run the tool again.

sign-in.why: first pin (lane/c-delivery, architecture audit 2026-11-19 item 3): set/v0.2.143 (8680e0992) bundled and minified, fonts self-hosted, 12 modules / 196.4 KB gzip to sign-in and 21 / 851.9 KB to town; the same site as written (--deliver plain) is 42 / 263.7 KB and 621 / 2,497.0 KB

lane/b-ui-buttons (7d0726992, 354fac7ad, UI audit #3) merged into set/v0.2.143 after the first pin: one button system painted in shell.css (+85 lines, three tokens), the controls block moved there from hunt.css, framed presses across the windows; every stylesheet loads with the page, so +1.0 KB gzip to sign-in and +1.2 KB to town. Measured identical on be2de0e71 (the set before origin/main v0.2.142 merged in) and on the merge (stamps only)

set/v0.2.143 after the second pin (293a58b21): lane/b-morrow-kit's art classes in src/data/world/art-budget.js (+81 B gzip, the sign-in backdrop's camera reads it) and the merged lanes' own code on the game half: elements-6b abilities + hunt roles (+477 B), first-hours-bugs launcher, chronicle, live-events, sheet, away text (+590 B), the Trophy Room hold in home-sections (+86 B), morrow maps and terrain (+125 B). Each is a feature's own code or data, nothing a later import() could carry; measured per module with --deliver minify on 293a58b21 and e596bbb08

Luck v3.1 (lane/d-luck-build): the Lucky Rivet and eight Lucky ring rows and their flavour lines (items.js, item-descriptions.js), Luck's text rows (text/luck.js, shop.js, jewel.js) on the one text table, and its client: luck-sections.js, the sheet's Magic Find bar, the loot plan's Salvage/Use lines and Dispatch answer, the Lucky job rows, the return card's Magic Find line
